papers.title: Vigilance profiles at sleep onset in patients with difficulty initiating sleep, with and without depressive or anxiety symptoms
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of polysomnography in 2,952 sleep-clinic patients found that difficulty initiating sleep (DIS) is characterized by more continuous EEG-based vigilance during wakefulness and sleep onset, while the sleep-onset period duration itself differed only marginally; depressive symptoms were linked to a less wake-like sleep-onset period despite more severe insomnia complaints.

papers.title: Multichannel Polysomnographic Sensor Fusion for Automatic Sleep Stage Classification.
papers.summary: Proposed a dual-stream deep learning model for automatic five-class sleep staging from multimodal polysomnographic signals (EEG, EOG, EMG), using time-domain and time-frequency features fused with a bidirectional LSTM. Subject-wise cross-validation yielded 91.5% accuracy and a Cohen's kappa of 0.829, with a lightweight variant achieving 88.8% accuracy.

papers.title: Real-time noise cancellation for EEG monitoring and brain-computer interfaces
papers.summary: We present rtSOUND, a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm for EEG noise suppression that uses a spatial filter updated asynchronously to clean each streamed sample. Validated on TMS-EEG and resting-state data from 25 healthy subjects, rtSOUND consistently improved SNR across metrics, particularly for low-SNR channels, while retaining waveforms in high-quality channels and processing data at 5 kHz.

papers.title: Quantifying Subject-Identity Variance in Spectral EEG Features and Its Role in Machine Learning Evaluation Leakage.
papers.summary: Quantified subject-identity variance in spectral EEG features using a longitudinal dataset and four public datasets, showing that subject identity accounts for substantial variance and can inflate downstream clinical classification when evaluation uses naive segment-level splits. The findings support subject-wise evaluation and confound diagnostics in EEG machine-learning studies.

papers.title: Gradient-Free Filter Importance for Structured Pruning of Compact EEG Networks.
papers.summary: Compared five filter-importance criteria for structured pruning of compact EEG networks across four datasets, two paradigms, and two architectures. Found that after fine-tuning, ablation-based SSA and first-order Taylor are statistically equivalent on EEGNet, but SSA is the best gradient-free criterion for quantized (8-bit) EEGNet where gradients are undefined, and pruning schedule and fine-tuning matter more than criterion choice.

papers.title: Between patterns and predictions: Interpretable latent EEG representations for clinical insights.
papers.summary: Applied a pretrained Universal Map of EEG latent embedding, without retraining, to three independent clinical cohorts (cardiac arrest n=575, subarachnoid hemorrhage n=100, routine EEG n=141). Trajectory-derived geometric and temporal features discriminated outcome in cardiac arrest (ROC-AUC 0.83) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (ROC-AUC 0.76) and distinguished physiological from pathological routine EEGs (ROC-AUC 0.93).

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.summary: This study introduces concept bottleneck models for EEG pathology detection that use analytically computed clinical EEG biomarkers (e.g., band power, spectral ratios, phase locking values) as an interpretable bottleneck. The models approach black-box baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but show lower performance on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%), with a pure CBM variant exhibiting concept fidelity concerns mitigated by increasing concept loss weight.

papers.title: Feature-Based Machine-Learning Spike Marking in Signal and Source Space EEG: A Proof-of-Principle Case Study of Focal Epilepsy.
papers.summary: Proof-of-principle case study trained artificial neural networks to classify interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) from EEG in signal and source space for focal epilepsy. Feature extraction improved performance; highest accuracy (0.98) was in signal space with Katz Fractional Dimension (KFD), while source space models reached 0.84; annotation variability among experts framed ANN performance within inter-expert agreement range.

papers.title: An Interpretable Framework for Identifying EEG Spectral Biomarkers of Pathological Brain Aging.
papers.summary: Proposed an interpretable EEG framework integrating explainable machine learning and probabilistic modeling to identify spectral biomarkers of pathological brain aging across two independent datasets including cognitively normal and Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and frontotemporal dementia patients. The theta/alpha ratio emerged as a representative biomarker showing reduced temporal stability and broader empirical distributions in most neurodegenerative groups compared to controls.

papers.title: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.
papers.summary: Developed a two-stage framework that first classifies normal versus sleep-deprived rest EEG with a CNN-BiLSTM, then feeds data into lightweight CNNs to recognize four affective states. It achieved 95.96% normal/sleep-deprived accuracy under window-level splitting but only 70.46% under subject-independent cross-validation, with affective-state accuracies of 93.40% (normal sleep) and 90.95% (sleep-deprived) under window-level splitting and about 39% under subject-independent cross-validation.

papers.title: Progressive neurodegeneration of the locus coeruleus drives rapid eye movement sleep fragmentation
papers.summary: Using progressive Caspase-3-mediated locus coeruleus ablation in adult female DBH-Cre mice with longitudinal sleep recordings and calcium fiber photometry, this study showed that graded LC degeneration caused REM sleep fragmentation emerging at mild (~25%) neuronal loss, increased light-hour REM sleep and declining REM theta power at moderate (~50%) loss, and blunted state-dependent LC calcium activity.

papers.title: FedCareX: Trust-Aware Federated Transformer for Wearable IoT Seizure Prediction.
papers.summary: FedCareX is a trust-aware federated Transformer framework for wearable IoT seizure prediction that uses a montage-agnostic tokenizer, adaptive reliability aggregation based on annotation quality, gradient consistency, and probe-set agreement, plus a sparsified error-feedback codec. On a five-centre wearable corpus, it achieved 83.1±0.6% sensitivity with 0.38 false predictions per hour and reduced uplink volume by 22.1×; on a scalp benchmark with 23 patient clients, it reached 92.8±0.4% sensitivity with 0.22 false predictions per hour.

papers.title: Epileptic seizure onset early warning using a lightweight multimodal self-explainable neural network.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: Developed lightweight multimodal self-explainable neural networks (learned and identity variants) for real-time epileptic seizure onset early warning using EEG from drug-resistant epilepsy patients, achieving 96.524% and 95.328% accuracy with high stability (~99.88%) and low explicitness values.

papers.title: A Pilot Study of the Feasibility of In-Ear EEG for Long-Term Temporal Lobe Brain Wave Monitoring.
papers.summary: This pilot study evaluated SeizEAR, a standardized paste-based in-ear EEG system, for long-term temporal lobe monitoring in five healthy adults over ~3-hour sessions. In-ear recordings showed moderate band-dependent correspondence with ipsilateral temporal scalp EEG, strongest in delta and alpha bands, with high comfort ratings and no adverse events.

papers.title: CSTO-Net: Cross-View Spectral-Transport and Topology-Operator Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed CSTO-Net, a cross-view spectral-transport and topology-operator network for EEG emotion recognition that couples differential entropy node attributes with Pearson-correlation and phase-locking-value connectivity graphs via optimal-transport routing and a skew-symmetric graph-operator commutator. It reported 93.95% valence and 94.97% arousal accuracy on DEAP and 93.12% on SEED under subject-dependent splits, with strong subject-independent and leave-one-subject-out performance.

papers.title: Fear-EEG-AI: A Conceptual and Operational Framework for Designing EEG-AI Systems for the Inference of Fear-Compatible Neurophysiological States.
papers.summary: This paper introduces the Fear-EEG-AI Framework, a technology-independent architecture for designing, validating, and deploying EEG-AI systems to infer fear-compatible neurophysiological states, organized into three hierarchical levels and six principles, with eight observable dimensions, the Fear-EEG-AI Alignment Index (FAI), and five validation evidence levels. Applied to eight eligible studies by two raters, the rubric achieved 67.2% exact agreement (quadratic-weighted κ=0.741; ICC(2,1)=0.744), but the index is reported as a descriptor of methodological documentation rather than a ranking of implementations.

papers.title: Balancing Local and Global Dependencies in EEG Emotion Recognition via Multi-Scale Hybrid Attention.
papers.summary: The paper proposes DSFConformer, an EEG emotion recognition framework that integrates multi-scale spatiotemporal convolution, Dynamic Sparse Feature Fusion (DSFF), and a Lite Transformer for global dependency modeling. On the SEED dataset, DSFConformer achieved 96.08% accuracy under chronological block-wise segment-level cross-validation and 78.81% under a stricter trial-wise protocol, statistically comparable to EEG-Conformer, with ablations showing that multi-scale convolution and DSFF drive recognition gains while the Lite Transformer mainly improves computational efficiency.

papers.title: A jointly optimized hybrid framework for epileptic EEG artifact classification.
papers.summary: Proposed a hybrid epileptic EEG artifact classification framework fusing handcrafted temporal-spectral-entropy features with lightweight ResNet-LSTM deep features, using Class Neighborhood Discrimination feature selection and Adaptive Seagull Optimization to jointly tune selector and random forest classifier. It achieved 99.30% accuracy on the constructed dataset and 98.15% on an independent clinical test set, outperforming representative baselines.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo for Bayesian spectral analysis.
papers.summary: Proposed a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo sampler for parallel Bayesian spectral deconvolution and model selection, reaching free-energy accuracy comparable to optimized CPU replica exchange Monte Carlo up to approximately 37x faster, validated on simulated XPS/XRD-like data and real spectra.

papers.title: Context Shapes Alpha-Band Electrophysiological Signatures Under Psilocybin
papers.summary: Analyzed the largest psilocybin EEG dataset to date (n=56) across movie viewing, eyes-closed rest, guided meditation, and music listening, finding that psilocybin decreased alpha power, increased gamma power and alpha peak frequency, and reduced alpha-band functional connectivity, with structured sensory contexts attenuating or reversing these connectivity changes.

papers.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
papers.summary: Conducted a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 57 studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals, mapping analytical pipelines across signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. It concluded that observed coupling varies with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and lag handling rather than being a single quantity, supporting framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting.

papers.title: Neuroelectrophysiological correlates of extended cessation of consciousness in advanced meditators: A multimodal EEG and MEG study
papers.summary: First electrophysiological study of 'extended cessation' (intentional suppression of consciousness) in five advanced meditators using concurrent EEG and MEG. EC significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five participants without consistent effects on Lempel-Ziv complexity or power, suggesting neural signatures distinct from deep sleep and anesthesia.

papers.title: Video EEG in pediatric epilepsy: Diagnostic significance and association between frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity.
papers.summary: Compared video EEG (VEEG) to routine EEG for diagnosing childhood epilepsy, finding VEEG had higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value (p < 0.05). Among 80 children with epilepsy, increased relative power of delta and theta bands and higher discharge indices correlated positively with cognitive impairment severity, while alpha and beta power correlated negatively.

papers.title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
papers.summary: Intracranial stereoelectroencephalography in eight epilepsy patients performing a near-threshold audiovisual detection task revealed a largely supramodal cortical detection code (including insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, superior temporal gyrus) whose multivariate decoders generalized across modalities, and a substantially supramodal confidence architecture including cross-modal confidence coding in sensory cortices.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.summary: This dual-brain EEG hyperscanning study examined leader-follower sensorimotor coordination in healthy adult pairs using a 2x2 design crossing Role with Mirroring versus Matching, proposing a tetradic framework for dyadic interaction. Neural analyses showed greater tonic power and phasic clusters during Matching, role-dependent anticipatory and post-response patterns, and information-theoretic signatures separating Leader-weighted predictive information from Follower-specific adaptive information, with sparse Synergy and Redundancy across specific cortical regions.

papers.title: Beyond EEG synchronization: methodological considerations in BOSSFRONT2.
papers.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
papers.summary: A letter commenting on methodological considerations in the BOSSFRONT2 study, arguing beyond EEG synchronization; no abstract or findings are available.

papers.title: Early caregiver mirroring predicts the emergence of action-unit-based facial representations in the infant brain.
papers.summary: Using EEG in 9- and 30-month-olds viewing dynamic facial expressions, the study found reliable encoding of facial action-unit structure at 30 months but not at the 9-month group level; individual 9-month AU encoding was predicted specifically by maternal mirroring of infant facial expressions at 2 months.

papers.title: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review examined 25 studies (2015–2026) on machine learning and deep learning for ADHD detection using multimodal physiological and behavioral biomarkers. Early multimodal fusion approaches often achieved diagnostic accuracies above 80%, but heterogeneity in data sources, modeling, and validation limited generalizability.

papers.title: Eyes-Open Fronto-Central Alpha Activity as an Electrophysiological Correlate of Working Memory in Children with Predominantly Inattentive ADHD.
papers.summary: In 45 children with ADHD, resting-state eyes-open frontocentral alpha power correlated positively with Working Memory Index scores only in the predominantly inattentive subtype (rho 0.535-0.582), with no such associations in combined ADHD or in eyes-closed recordings.

papers.title: Effects of Cannabidiol on Auditory Mismatch Negativity in Autistic Children
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a pilot double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 19 autistic children found only tentative evidence that 12 weeks of oral CBD shortened auditory MMN latency at FCz relative to placebo (not surviving FDR correction), while higher baseline MMN amplitude was associated with greater social-relating difficulties.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.summary: A bibliometric and thematic analysis of 3,479 machine learning and dementia publications found diagnostic classification as the predominant objective (55.0%) and structural MRI as the most common data modality (42.6%). The field is expanding toward multimodal, biomarker, prognostic, and language model applications.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of the Camel Heart: A Systematic Review of Evidence from Camelus dromedarius.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies on Camelus dromedarius found six direct ECG/telemetry studies reporting low resting heart rates and PR intervals of roughly 180-260 ms, with drug-associated rhythm abnormalities and substantial methodological heterogeneity precluding validated reference intervals.

papers.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study used concurrent TMS-EEG to test whether interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) is sensitive to GABAB receptor modulation and to replicate pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. In 29 participants, baclofen (a GABAB agonist) significantly decreased ISP over the motor region (p = 0.037) but not the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), indicating regional specificity.

papers.title: Clinical Outcomes and Treatment Characteristics of Seizure Threshold-Titrated Electroconvulsive Therapy in Schizophrenia: A 3.5-Year Retrospective Naturalistic Course-Level Study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective naturalistic study of 17 acute seizure threshold-titrated ECT courses in schizophrenia, median PANSS Positive Subscale scores fell from 45 to 16 and GAF rose from 44 to 60, with no MMSE deterioration, although motor and EEG seizure durations varied widely.

papers.title: Auditory-Olfactory Integration in Simulated Natural Environments Dissociates Neural and Subjective Responses in Visually Impaired Individuals.
papers.summary: In 20 visually impaired participants, the study combined field-recorded soundscapes with calibrated odor diffusion across five simulated landscape scenarios while recording occipital EEG α/β ratios and subjective ratings. It found a dissociation between subjective preference (favoring dynamic water sounds) and neurophysiological relaxation (highest α/β ratios with floral odors in low-amplitude acoustic contexts), with unfamiliar scents linked to stronger α/β elevation and stable baseline differences driving α/β variance.

papers.title: Reversal of refractory epilepsy in an adult with GAMT deficiency: A case report and comparative literature review.
papers.summary: Case report of the oldest known adult (52 years) with GAMT deficiency, presenting with refractory epilepsy and intellectual disability, who achieved complete seizure freedom and motor recovery after oral creatine supplementation. Comparative literature review found adults had higher prevalence of movement disorders (69.2% vs. 33.1%, p < 0.001) and a trend toward more epilepsy than pediatric patients.

papers.title: Reviewing Physiological Measures of Implicit Consumer Response to Food.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes 132 studies (2011–2026) applying autonomic (GSR, heart rate, pupil size, facial expression) and neural (EEG, fMRI) measures to implicit consumer responses to food. It reports that ANS indicators vary across products and often diverge from explicit liking, while fMRI implicates regions such as orbitofrontal and somatosensory cortex, supporting integration of self-report with physiological and neural measures.

papers.title: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.
papers.summary: The study built a dataset of 1173 excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectra of coal tar extracts covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and concentration gradients, comparing seven machine learning classifiers and a CNN-VAE quantification model. ResNet18 achieved ~90% classification accuracy, and the CNN-VAE reached RMSE and MAE as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively, for PAH quantification in complex matrices.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Dielectric Fingerprinting of Arrhythmogenic Substrates: A Precision Paradigm for Tissue Characterization Guided Cardiac Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This structured narrative review examined the scientific basis of myocardial dielectric properties in cardiac electrophysiology and assessed the current and potential role of artificial intelligence (AI) in interpreting dielectric and local impedance measurements. It found that AI algorithms trained primarily on myocardial dielectric or catheter-based local impedance data remain extremely scarce and mostly preclinical or ex vivo, whereas most clinically used AI in electrophysiology relies on ECG, intracardiac electrogram, image, or computational modeling data without dielectric inputs; standardization and prospective multicenter trials are needed before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Myocardial Fibrosis as an Arrhythmogenic Substrate: Integrating Genetics, Imaging and Invasive Electrophysiology for Sudden Death Risk Stratification.
papers.summary: This review integrates genetics, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (including late gadolinium enhancement), and invasive electroanatomic mapping to characterize myocardial fibrosis as an arrhythmogenic substrate for ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. It discusses how these modalities inform risk stratification and implantable cardioverter defibrillator decision-making.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
